title: Workplane local coordinates
content: Workplanes define a local 2D coordinate system in 3D space. Features are created relative to the active plane; face-based workplanes reduce manual global-coordinate calculations.

title: Workplane 2D construction
content: Use lines, arcs, circles, rectangles, polygons, splines and points to create closed wires or construction geometry before a 3D operation.

title: Workplane 3D construction
content: Create direct primitives or turn pending 2D wires into solids with extrude, revolve, sweep, loft and related operations.

title: Workplane selectors
content: Selectors filter topology such as faces, edges, vertices, wires and solids. Direction selectors like >Z and type selectors can drive subsequent features.

title: Construction geometry
content: Construction geometry locates features without becoming part of the final profile. A construction rectangle followed by vertices is a common hole-pattern technique.

title: Workplane stack and iteration
content: Each chained operation returns a Workplane with stack objects and a parent. Many methods apply automatically to every location or object on the stack.

title: Workplane chaining and tags
content: Fluent chains preserve parent links and shared modelling context. Tags let later operations return to a named state or select from it.

title: Context solid and pending wires
content: The first solid becomes the context solid. Later additive or subtractive operations search the parent chain for it; combine=False keeps new solids separate. Pending wires feed 3D operations.

title: Sketch face-based API and modes
content: Sketch face operations combine geometry in-place using additive, subtractive, intersect, replace or construction modes. Sketch selection must be reset explicitly because Sketch has no history chain.

title: Sketch edge-based API
content: Build individual segments and arcs, close or connect them, then call assemble() to convert edge geometry into faces before face operations.

title: Sketch convex hull
content: The experimental hull operation creates a convex hull for supported straight segments and circles.

title: Sketch constraints and solver
content: Experimental sketch constraints support fixed points, coincidence, angle, length, distance, radius, orientation and arc angle for segments and arcs; solve before assemble.

title: Sketch and Workplane integration
content: Create sketches in-place with Workplane.sketch().finalize(), or reuse an existing Sketch with placeSketch(). Sketches can drive extrude, twistExtrude, revolve, sweep, cuts and loft.

title: Sketch reuse, offsets, import and export
content: Sketches can be placed at multiple stack locations, combined, offset, lofted between, and imported or exported for reuse.

title: Assembly parameters and reusable components
content: Define shared dimensions first and create reusable component functions. Add named component instances to a cq.Assembly so parts remain identifiable.

title: Assembly object locations
content: Parts may be placed explicitly with Location values. Explicit placement is often the simplest robust approach when exact constraint solving is unnecessary.

title: Assembly constraints
content: Assembly constraints include Point, Axis, Plane, PointInPlane, PointOnLine, FixedPoint, FixedRotation and FixedAxis. Name or tag mating topology, constrain it, then solve.

title: Assembly colors and hierarchy
content: Assembly items and nested subassemblies can have names, colors, materials, metadata and relative locations.

title: Assembly export
content: Assemblies can be converted to compounds or exported in supported assembly-aware formats. Preserve names and hierarchy when the chosen format supports them.
